seen_animation: A small black-line bird with an oval body floats on the water line just below the bank of grey trees and grass, slightly left of center. In frames 1-12 its front end ends in a short folded hook at the right of the body, as if the neck is bent down to the water, and the bird drifts slightly left (about x=200 in frame 1 to about x=175 by frames 9-12 within each panel). The grey scenery shifts a little left over frames 1-8 and then holds. In frame 13 the neck comes up and points forward-right; in frames 14-16 the neck rises further into an upright curve with a small head at the top, while the body stays in place.
seen_film: A white swan floats on a pond in front of a reed bank and trees, slightly left of center near the far shore. In frames 1-12 its neck is bent down with the head at or in the water, feeding, while it drifts slowly left. The camera framing shifts slightly. In frame 13 the swan raises its head into an upright S-curved neck, and in frames 14-16 it holds the head up, facing right, with little change in position.
named_subject: A swan (long-necked water bird) floating on a pond, first feeding with its head down, then raising its neck.
evidence: Frames 1-12 in both: the bird sits at the same height on the water line, slightly left of center, with neck bent down, drifting a short distance left (animation frame 1 about x=200, frame 9 about x=175; film frame 1 about x=200, frame 9 about x=180). The head-up change happens at frame 13 in both. Frames 14-16 in both: neck upright and curved, head facing right, body nearly stationary. Body oval, inner wing line, and neck stroke follow c.png. Weakness: in frames 1-12 the down-turned head is a tight tangle of short strokes at the front of the body that reads more as a knot than a neck dipping into water; in frame 13 the animated neck points forward at a low angle, while the film's swan is already fully upright, so the lift lags by about one frame.
primary_gap: During frames 1-12 the bent-down neck and head are drawn as a small cramped scribble at the front of the body, so the feeding pose does not read clearly as the doodle's long neck curved down into the water.
closes_when: In frames 1-12 the neck is drawn as one visible curved stroke of the doodle's neck length arching forward and down so the small head touches the water line in front of the body, and in frame 13 the neck is already mostly upright as in the film.
protect: The placement and leftward drift matching the film, the head-lift timing at frame 13, the stable body without popping or doubling, the doodle's oval body with inner wing line and simple single-weight strokes, and the restrained grey scenery.
identity_gap: The body matches the doodle, but during the head-down frames the long neck that defines the doodle is compressed into a short hook, so the drawing is recognizable mainly from frame 13 on.
